referents.why: 'which he had appointed for Pharaoh' (qatal, third masculine singular) names the one who sent the frogs against Pharaoh: the LORD (Exo.8.1 commands the frogs; the plague is His). Moses and Pharaoh are the other masculine singular candidates, and neither sent the plague.

links.why: wayyiqtol: after Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, Moses cried out. The sequence is on the verse's narrative line.
Reverses the order: cl0 (they left) comes first in the text, and the then link runs forward from it.
'the frogs which he had appointed for Pharaoh' is a relative clause inside the noun phrase that is the object of cried out. The link reads: cl2 sits inside cl1.

cant_tell.what: whether Moses's crying out carries out Pharaoh's imperative 'pray to the LORD' (Exo.8.4 cl2) as a fulfilment
cant_tell.why: fulfils needs a pro-form report (asah + ken) with no named subject. The verse gives the prayer in plain words, so it is a reading for review and is not recorded as a link.
